settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The Javadoc at lines 54-76 warns ZipArchiveInputStream is deliberately laxer than ZipFile and may return incomplete/unknown data; this buffering is a documented consequence rather than an obvious defect.
RELEASE-NOTES.txt 38-40 (COMPRESS-454) shows this code was already the subject of a recent fix, suggesting the maintainers consider the behaviour intentional for STORED+DD entries.
Stored-entry buffering is only reached when lastStoredEntry == null (511-514) and the entry is genuinely STORED.
candidates.description: In ZipArchiveInputStream.readStoredEntry() (lines 877-906) the stream reads until it detects a local-file-header / central-directory-header / data-descriptor signature and writes every byte it consumes into a ByteArrayOutputStream (bos). There is no upper bound tied to the declared entry size or to any configurable memory limit: the while(!done) loop at 885-902 keeps reading into the in-memory buffer as long as no signature appears and the underlying stream keeps returning data (r > 0 at 886-891). The byte array is then materialised again via bos.toByteArray() at 904 and wrapped in a ByteArrayInputStream at 905. The call chain is read() (428-473) -> readStored (508-542) -> readStoredEntry(), so this path is exercised whenever an entry is STORED, uses a data descriptor, and the caller enabled stored entries with data descriptors. bufferContainsSignature (920-950) only terminates the loop when a matching signature is found, and cacheBytesRead (961-971) moves un-cached bytes back to the front of the buffer without imposing a cap. This is a classic data-driven memory-consumption pattern: a crafted (or simply large) archive can cause the library to buffer the whole decompressed entry in heap memory. Confidence is limited because the read spans do not show who sets allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor, nor whether callers cap input size; the class's own Javadoc (54-76) documents this streamer as the less strict option.
missing_evidence: The value of ZipArchiveOutputStream.BUFFER_SIZE referenced at 886 and implicitly at 97/121.
Whether any caller in the repository (ArchiveStreamFactory, examples) enables allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor.
MemoryLimitException usage (its source was not read) and whether it is wired into this path.
ZipUtil.setNameAndCommentFromExtraFields / canHandleEntryData behaviour, since these gate parts of the same entry handling.
preconditions: Caller constructs ZipArchiveInputStream and enables stored entries with a data descriptor (the constructor flag at 210-222 / 218-219).
Archive contains a STORED entry whose general-purpose bit indicates a data descriptor and whose payload is large and/or contains no LFH/CFH/DD signature bytes.
Caller reads through read(...) into readStored(...) without an external size/quotum limit.
candidates.title: Unbounded in-memory caching of STORED entries with data descriptor in ZipArchiveInputStream.readStoredEntry

counter_evidence: security-reports.xml:33-39 explicitly states the page lists vulnerabilities in released versions, so absence of 1.18 entries is expected for a snapshot.
Release notes only say a bug was fixed, not that a new issue was introduced.
candidates.description: The build declares version 1.18-SNAPSHOT (pom.xml:27) while the release notes only cover up to 1.17 (RELEASE-NOTES.txt:8-58), and the security-reports page only lists fixes through 1.16 (CVE-2018-1324) and 1.4.1 (CVE-2012-2098) (security-reports.xml:57-111). The in-progress changes include RELEASE-NOTES.txt:38-40 ('ZipArchiveInputStream failed to read some files with stored entries using a data descriptor', COMPRESS-454), which is exactly the code region read at lines 877-971. Newer, not-yet-released code for a parsing path handling attacker-controlled archives has not been included in the documented security-report history read in this review. This is reported as context/uncertainty rather than as a defect: the read material does not contain any claim of a flaw in the new code, and the security-reports page is a documentation artefact that is expected to lag the unreleased snapshot.
missing_evidence: changes.xml content for the 1.18 development cycle (file listed but not read in the reviewed spans).
The actual diff of the COMPRESS-454 fix relative to 1.17.
preconditions: Consumption of the 1.18-SNAPSHOT artefacts rather than a released version.
Use of the reworked STORED+data-descriptor handling in ZipArchiveInputStream.
candidates.title: Potential 1.18-SNAPSHOT state: ZIP stored-entry-with-data-descriptor path recently reworked without released-version security review
